recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not remove DocumentReference.content.attachment for FHIR-12949; any further narrowing of Attachment summary metadata or adding practiceSetting should be handled by a current-version work-group issue when applied.
issue_request: FHIR-12949 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2. It requested a minimal UI-list _summary subset for DocumentReference rather than returning document content, with the final accepted set covering status, docStatus, type, class, subject, author, description, context.period, content.format, content.attachment.contentType, content.attachment.language, identifier, masterIdentifier, indexed, and securityLabel/confidentiality.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 94e532a611046fcdc40df2d7d28457eeb7dad3a6 explicitly lists GF#12949 in a DocumentReference block-vote commit and updated the then-authoritative DocumentReference spreadsheet summary markers. It retained metadata summary flags and removed several non-list summary flags, while keeping content and content.attachment as wrappers needed to expose selected Attachment metadata.
additional_context: DocumentReference is active in source/fhir.ini. Current source uses evolved names: class is category, indexed is date, context.period is period, content.format is content.profile.value[x], and masterIdentifier is folded into identifier. Current ElementDefinition summary guidance excludes Attachment.data while Attachment.contentType and Attachment.language remain summary datatype properties. Later current-version evolution added other summary metadata such as version, modality, bodyStructure, context, and relatesTo. FHIR-54538 later requests practiceSetting in summary but is only Resolved - change required/Ready_to_Apply and was not in this default applied/published source-edit scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source carries forward the FHIR-12949 result on the accepted current equivalents, and removing the content.attachment wrapper would either lose accepted Attachment metadata or conflict with current summary semantics that exclude Attachment.data instead of excluding the wrapper.
